Hi PS, (prepare for many words - you asked for thought provoking) I wouldn't beat yourself up too much about the USDCAD trade. You took it out for a small profit! You will be better prepared next time I have no doubt.

With regards to your price read in your last post. The H1 stuff looks like textbook RTM to me with consideration to the HTF which I love. This helps me too buddy:)

For your D1 chart. Sure that is a valid FTR and expecting some sort of bounce is only sensible, AND there was a 100 pip long trade from it too! But, I think it's at this point when you're looking at a too good to be true daily level with compression approach and you're so zoomed out that it's actually time to start consulting the Weekly and Monthly charts for additional clues and PA you would expect to see.

When price falls as quickly as it came up you don't want to be caught trying to catch falling knives, check the weekly out, eeep! So you have to do something different from what the herd is doing (I am assuming they are trying to pick the bottom). When you are in the moment, put yourself in a neutral position, one engulf at a time, and instead of looking for reversal PA exclusively, look for the "how do I get it in on this bear move!" Okay so maybe a chart or two will explain this better..

Please keep the weekly in mind for the upcoming story! Please note that 1 horizontal line I have marked on the WK chart and think about what that would mean if it were engulfed with decent PA.

Anyway I want to tell the Daily story with numbers and letters for reference. -All demand/supply zones have been marked with a number. -All lines I have drawn in have been marked a..b..c..d..etc. (What do these lines mean? Most likely an engulfed FTR or Decision or FL or you get it:))

NZDUSD Weekly

NZDUSD Daily

Zone 1. Supply, and 'bears' in control.

Zone 2. Your valid FTR, it does a lot of cool stuff! It sets in motion some very 'bullish' prices, not only engulfing the previous 3 days of PA it sets up zone 3, which brings about line b as a price point of interest in the future.

Zone 3. Buy buy buy. Engulfs line a, engulfs supply zone 1. A retest of this area would have been a beaut, but price ran away.

Zone 4. Well at this point price has already engulfed zone 3/line b and its suggesting price wants lower. It reloads at some decision made on LTF @ line c and creates a new supply zone with an engulf of line d and down into our valid FTR. (Wow that was wordy, its wordy because this is some critical PA in the context of this chart and the weekly)

At this point I stopped drawing zones

Line e. The engulf of line e was so critical in terms of trapping a huge amount of buyers, as this is the type of PA you look at and go "YES YES YES BUY TIME!" If you didn't have zone 4 drawn in (what a FO level right?), you would have no idea why price didn't continue on further and by the time you realised it you would have been in heavy draw down when zone 2 finally got broken.

Line f. Engulfed. It should come at no surprise now that it seems less and less likely that there is going to be a reversal.

Weekly. Now look back at the weekly. Lower low..lower low...lower low...Do you see why I drew the 1 horizontal line?

Anyway that concludes the story. There's obviously a lot more we could have spoken about here but I just wanted to remind you how important it is to actually have a neutral position and using each new engulf as a new piece to the puzzle you didn't previosuly have..

Cheers,

SP

I've been working through this recently (as in the last 24 hours or so) too. What brought it to my attention was a few posts I exchanged with Michal238 yesterday and then seeing this post where IF says: "Start with getting to understand the PAZ. There's tons of info about it around lately. Think about where to look for trades - At the edge of the PAZ and nowhere else"

So I started thinking about FTR PAZ's. Price moves around in consolidation limited by the FTR and a cap both of which are often tradeable on FTB. Then it either breaks the consolidation by breaking the FTR in the direction it came from or by breaking the cap and continuing on - either way price creates a new FTR in a new PAZ, and when drawn on a chart, it looks like the boxing you've drawn in post 321. Sometimes it can be a bit difficult to find the exact extents of the box or when several overlap, and I imagine this is a bit harder still when trying "to box" the right edge in real-time. But step-by-step we'll get there.

A traditional supply/demand trader could probably also argue that you've just boxed a bunch of bases of RBR, DBD, DBR, and RBD's. But with that mindset you ignore the FTR that starts a new box (aka: PAZ) and you've eliminated the precision for where to actually enter a trade, which means increased risk and decreased reward.

It's truly amazing how all this stuff fits together. Hopefully soon it will fit without so much thinking so that I can trade on instincts (aka: Read the Market.) Again, step-by-step... Thanks for posting!
